justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Enables high-repetition stepping; not superior to dose-matched conventional in Cochrane review. May benefit very early, low-function stroke.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Device-specific manufacturer training; requires institutional access to robotic gait system.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Limited by expensive equipment; applicable in neuro gait training at select academic or research centers only.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Very limited insurance coverage; mostly research settings; some WC; primarily institutional or self-pay.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Very limited employer demand; primarily research centers and specialized neuro rehabilitation hospitals.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Novel technology appeals; some patients prefer robotic to manual assistance.
justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Hocoma and similar robotics vendors employ clinical specialists for deployment and training.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Narrow but consistent vendor demand for trained clinicians.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Modest premium for robotics vendor clinical roles.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Hands-on with complex robotic gait systems builds technical literacy.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Some neuro/SCI families will pay cash for robotic gait training, but the population is small and competing with research centers offering it free.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Premium pricing is possible per session, but the device cost destroys margins unless you have high volume.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Owning a Lokomat or similar is genuinely differentiating in a regional market; few clinics have one.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Technicians and assistants can deliver robotic gait training under supervision, making this more scalable than personality-based methods.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Awareness is rising in SCI/stroke communities but still niche; demand is concentrated, not broad.
justifications.business.efficiency: Capital cost ($300K+) and training time make this one of the least efficient credentials to acquire.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Not a formal credential but signals neuro-tech expertise; helpful but not decisive for hiring/promotion.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Robotic gait training has a substantial and growing publication record; strong vehicle for faculty research.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Directly relevant to neuro curriculum, lab demonstrations, and emerging tech content in DPT programs.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Multiple RCTs and systematic reviews exist; evidence is mixed but the literature base is solid.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Occasionally preferred at programs with neuro-tech labs, but not a common job-posting requirement.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Requires institutional access to expensive equipment; very poor on a time/cost basis for individuals.
